subproblems.title: The sector box Z_s is open and the polar map (|x|, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩)) is C¹ on the half-space ⟨x,a⟩ > 0
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π := Q.starProjection, a, e ∈ ℝ^P and s ∈ ℝ. Put f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩) (real division, t/0 = 0), F̃(x) := (|x|, f(x)) ∈ ℝ × ℝ, Ω := {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0} and Z_s := {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s, |f(x)| < s, |x − πx| < s|x|}. Then Z_s is open and F̃ is C¹ on Ω (ContDiffOn ℝ 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (s : ℝ), IsOpen {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖} ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x : Euclid P => (‖x‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a))) {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. ⟨·,·⟩ is the inner product of ℝ^P = Euclid P; π := Q.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto Q, a continuous linear map (Q is finite-dimensional, hence closed). Ω := {x : 0 < ⟨x,a⟩}; q(x) := ⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩ (real division, t/0 = 0); f := arctan ∘ q; F̃ := (|·|, f) : ℝ^P → ℝ × ℝ; Z_s := {x : 0 < ⟨x,a⟩ ∧ ||x| − 1| < s ∧ |f(x)| < s ∧ |x − πx| < s|x|}. No hypothesis on Q, a, e, s is needed.
1. (Ω is open.) Ω is the set where the continuous function x ↦ ⟨x,a⟩ is strictly greater than the constant 0, hence open (`isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_id.inner continuous_const)`).
2. (Points of Ω.) Every x ∈ Ω satisfies ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0, and x ≠ 0 because ⟨0,a⟩ = 0.
3. (f is C¹ on Ω.) Fix x ∈ Ω. The maps y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩ and y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩ are continuous linear, hence C^∞ (`ContDiff.inner ℝ contDiff_id contDiff_const`). Their quotient q is C^∞ at x because the denominator ⟨x,a⟩ is nonzero (step 2; `ContDiffAt.div`). Real.arctan is C^∞ on ℝ (`Real.contDiff_arctan`), so f = arctan ∘ q is C^∞, in particular C¹, at x, hence C¹ within Ω at x. Since x ∈ Ω was arbitrary, f is ContDiffOn ℝ 1 on Ω; in particular f is continuous on Ω.
4. (F̃ is C¹ on Ω.) Fix x ∈ Ω. The norm of a real inner product space is C^∞ at every nonzero point (`contDiffAt_norm ℝ`), and x ≠ 0 by step 2, so |·| is C¹ at x and hence within Ω at x. Together with step 3, the pair F̃ = (|·|, f) is C¹ within Ω at x (`ContDiffWithinAt.prodMk`). Hence ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F̃ Ω, which is the second conjunct.
5. (Z_s is open.) Let B := Ω ∩ {x : |f(x)| < s}. The function x ↦ |f(x)| is continuous on Ω (step 3), Ω is open (step 1) and (−∞, s) is open, so B = Ω ∩ (|f|)⁻¹((−∞, s)) is open (`ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage`). The sets A₁ := {x : ||x| − 1| < s} and A₃ := {x : |x − πx| < s|x|} are open, each being the set where one continuous function on ℝ^P is strictly smaller than another (`isOpen_lt`; |·| and π are continuous). Unfolding the definitions, x ∈ Z_s iff (0 < ⟨x,a⟩ and |f(x)| < s) and ||x| − 1| < s and |x − πx| < s|x|, i.e. Z_s = B ∩ A₁ ∩ A₃. A finite intersection of open sets is open, so Z_s is open (if s ≤ 0 it is empty, which is consistent). This is the first conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ω = {⟨x,a⟩ > 0} is open and its points are nonzero with ⟨x,a⟩ ≠ 0.
arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩) is C¹ (hence continuous) on Ω: quotient of linear maps with nonvanishing denominator composed with the smooth arctan.
|·| is C^∞ away from 0, so F̃ = (|·|, f) is ContDiffOn ℝ 1 on Ω.
Z_s = (Ω ∩ |f|⁻¹(−∞,s)) ∩ {||x|−1| < s} ∩ {|x−πx| < s|x|} is a finite intersection of open sets (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage, isOpen_lt).

subproblems.title: Area-formula Jacobian of the polar map along a 2-plane containing the radial direction
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q and T linear subspaces of ℝ^P, and a, e, x ∈ ℝ^P with dim Q = 2, a, e ∈ Q, |a| = |e| = 1, ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, dim T = 2 and p_T(x) = x (p_T := T.starProjection). Let F̃(y) := (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)) ∈ ℝ × ℝ, D := DF̃(x) (fderiv), (u_i)_{i < dim T} := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T, and Γ the dim T × dim T matrix Γ_ij := (Du_i)_1(Du_j)_1 + (Du_i)_2(Du_j)_2. Then sqrt(det Γ) = |p_T(⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a)| / |Q.starProjection x|².
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e x : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → 0 < inner ℝ x a → Module.finrank ℝ T = 2 → T.starProjection x = x → Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ T) => (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => (‖y‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a))) x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T i)).1 * (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => (‖y‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a))) x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T j)).1 + (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => (‖y‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a))) x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T i)).2 * (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => (‖y‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y a))) x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T j)).2)) = ‖T.starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, facts (F1)–(F3) and step 4 (Jacobian), made explicit in coordinates. Notation: α := ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, β := ⟨x,e⟩, A := αe − βa (this is Ax), ρ := α² + β², x̂ := x/|x|, g := A/ρ (this is ∇f(x)), F̃(y) := (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)), D := fderiv ℝ F̃ x, (u_k)_{k ∈ Fin(dim T)} := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T (vectors of T viewed in ℝ^P), Γ_kl := (Du_k)_1(Du_l)_1 + (Du_k)_2(Du_l)_2, p_T := T.starProjection, π := Q.starProjection. Goal: sqrt(det Γ) = |p_T A|/|πx|².
1. (F1: πx = αa + βe and |πx|² = ρ > 0.) The family (a, e) is orthonormal (|a| = |e| = 1, ⟨a,e⟩ = 0), hence linearly independent, and span{a,e} ⊆ Q because a, e ∈ Q; since dim span{a,e} = 2 = dim Q, span{a,e} = Q (`Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq`, `finrank_span_eq_card`). The vector w₀ := αa + βe lies in Q, and x − w₀ is orthogonal to every w = c₀a + c₁e ∈ Q: ⟨x − w₀, c₀a + c₁e⟩ = c₀(α − α) + c₁(β − β) = 0, using ⟨a,a⟩ = ⟨e,e⟩ = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0. Hence πx = w₀ (`Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero`), and expanding ⟨w₀, w₀⟩ gives |πx|² = α² + β² = ρ. Since α > 0, ρ ≥ α² > 0.
2. (F2: A ⊥ x.) ⟨A, x⟩ = α⟨e,x⟩ − β⟨a,x⟩ = αβ − βα = 0.
3. (F3: the derivative of F̃ at x.) x ≠ 0 since ⟨x,a⟩ > 0 = ⟨0,a⟩. (a) The norm is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ ⟨x,v⟩/|x|: |y| = sqrt(|y|²), the derivative of |y|² at x is v ↦ 2⟨x,v⟩ (`hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq`), and sqrt is differentiable at |x|² ≠ 0 with derivative 1/(2|x|) (`HasFDerivAt.sqrt`). (b) y ↦ ⟨y,e⟩ and y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩ are linear with derivatives v ↦ ⟨e,v⟩ and v ↦ ⟨a,v⟩ (`innerSL`, `real_inner_comm`). Since α ≠ 0, y ↦ ⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ has derivative v ↦ −⟨a,v⟩/α² (`hasFDerivAt_inv` composed with (b)), so by the product rule (`HasFDerivAt.mul`) q(y) := ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹ has derivative v ↦ ⟨e,v⟩/α − β⟨a,v⟩/α². (c) arctan has derivative 1/(1+t²) (`HasFDerivAt.arctan`), so y ↦ arctan(q(y)) has derivative v ↦ (1/(1 + β²/α²))·(⟨e,v⟩/α − β⟨a,v⟩/α²) = (α⟨e,v⟩ − β⟨a,v⟩)/(α² + β²) = ⟨A, v⟩/ρ. (d) The pair has the pair of derivatives (`HasFDerivAt.prodMk`); since y ↦ (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,a⟩)) coincides with y ↦ (|y|, arctan(⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹)) (t/s = t·s⁻¹; transfer with `HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq`), fderiv ℝ F̃ x equals this derivative (`HasFDerivAt.fderiv`). Hence for every v ∈ ℝ^P: (Dv)_1 = ⟨x,v⟩/|x| = ⟨x̂, v⟩ and (Dv)_2 = ⟨A, v⟩/ρ = ⟨g, v⟩ (the last identity is field arithmetic using α ≠ 0 and ρ ≠ 0).
4. (The 2×2 Gram determinant.) For k ∈ Fin(dim T) put a_k := ⟨x̂, u_k⟩ = ⟨x,u_k⟩/|x| and c_k := ⟨g, u_k⟩ = ⟨A,u_k⟩/ρ. By step 3, Γ_kl = a_k a_l + c_k c_l. Since dim T = 2 the index type is Fin 2 (state the identity for an index type Fin n with n = 2 and substitute n = 2, or reindex along finCongr with `Matrix.det_reindex_self`), and expanding with `Matrix.det_fin_two`:
   det Γ = (a_0² + c_0²)(a_1² + c_1²) − (a_0a_1 + c_0c_1)² = (a_0² + a_1²)(c_0² + c_1²) − (a_0c_0 + a_1c_1)² = (Σ_k a_k²)(Σ_k c_k²) − (Σ_k a_k c_k)²,
   because both middle expressions expand to (a_0c_1 − a_1c_0)² (Lagrange's identity). (In the parent's language: Γ = LᵀL for the 2×2 matrix L with rows (a_k)_k and (c_k)_k, so det Γ = (det L)²; in the orthonormal basis (x̂, τ) of T, det L = ±⟨∇f(x), τ⟩ = ±⟨g, τ⟩.)
5. (Parseval in T.) (u_k) is an orthonormal basis of T, so for y, z ∈ T: Σ_k ⟨y,u_k⟩² = |y|² and Σ_k ⟨y,u_k⟩⟨u_k,z⟩ = ⟨y,z⟩ (`OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_left`, `OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner`, applied in T to the elements x and p_T A of T). Moreover ⟨v, u_k⟩ = ⟨p_T v, u_k⟩ for every v ∈ ℝ^P, since v − p_T v ⊥ T ∋ u_k (`Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero`). The hypothesis p_T x = x means x ∈ T (`Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff`). Therefore:
   (i) Σ_k a_k² = |x|²/|x|² = 1;
   (ii) Σ_k a_k c_k = (Σ_k ⟨x,u_k⟩⟨p_T A,u_k⟩)/(|x|ρ) = ⟨x, p_T A⟩/(|x|ρ) = ⟨p_T x, A⟩/(|x|ρ) = ⟨x, A⟩/(|x|ρ) = 0, using that p_T is self-adjoint (`Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right`) and step 2;
   (iii) Σ_k c_k² = Σ_k ⟨p_T A, u_k⟩²/ρ² = |p_T A|²/ρ².
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 5, det Γ = 1·|p_T A|²/ρ² − 0² = (|p_T A|/ρ)², so sqrt(det Γ) = |p_T A|/ρ (`Real.sqrt_sq`, as |p_T A|/ρ ≥ 0). By step 1, ρ = |πx|², so sqrt(det Γ) = |p_T(⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a)|/|Q.starProjection x|², as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so πx = ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e, |πx|² = ρ := ⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩² > 0, and A := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a ⊥ x.
For ⟨x,a⟩ > 0: fderiv F̃ x v = (⟨x,v⟩/|x|, ⟨A,v⟩/ρ) (norm via sqrt of norm², arctan ∘ (⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,a⟩⁻¹) via inverse, product and chain rules).
With a_k = ⟨x,u_k⟩/|x|, c_k = ⟨A,u_k⟩/ρ the Gram matrix is a_k a_l + c_k c_l and, as dim T = 2, det Γ = (Σa_k²)(Σc_k²) − (Σa_k c_k)² (det_fin_two, Lagrange).
Parseval in T with x ∈ T and ⟨v,u_k⟩ = ⟨p_T v,u_k⟩: Σa_k² = 1, Σa_k c_k = ⟨x,A⟩/(|x|ρ) = 0, Σc_k² = |p_T A|²/ρ².
Hence det Γ = (|p_T A|/ρ)² and sqrt(det Γ) = |p_T A|/|πx|².

subproblems.title: Carrier area formula for C¹ maps into ℝ × ℝ (transport through Euclid 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, M, Z ⊆ ℝ^P, F : ℝ^P → ℝ × ℝ and h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. Assume M is Borel and countably 2-rectifiable, H²(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K (H² := μHE[2]), Z is open, F is C¹ on Z, and h is a.e.-measurable for H²⌞M. For x ∈ ℝ^P let T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x, (u_i) := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T_x (indexed by Fin(dim T_x)), and J_F(x) := sqrt(det Γ(x)) with Γ(x)_ij := (DF(x)u_i)_1(DF(x)u_j)_1 + (DF(x)u_i)_2(DF(x)u_j)_2, DF(x) := fderiv ℝ F x. Then p ↦ Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ Z ∩ F⁻¹{p}} h(x) (tsum over the subtype) is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ, and ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} Σ_{x ∈ M ∩ Z ∩ F⁻¹{p}} h(x) dp = ∫_{M ∩ Z} ofReal(J_F(x))·h(x) dH²(x) (lower Lebesgue integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M Z : Set (Euclid P)) (F : Euclid P → ℝ × ℝ) (h : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable 2 M → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μHE[2] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → IsOpen Z → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 F Z → AEMeasurable h (μHE[2].restrict M) → AEMeasurable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ∑' x : ↥(M ∩ Z ∩ F ⁻¹' {p}), h x) volume ∧ ∫⁻ p : ℝ × ℝ, (∑' x : ↥(M ∩ Z ∩ F ⁻¹' {p}), h x) = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ Z, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane 2 M x)) => (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane 2 M x) i)).1 * (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane 2 M x) j)).1 + (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane 2 M x) i)).2 * (fderiv ℝ F x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (approxTangentPlane 2 M x) j)).2))) * h x ∂μHE[2]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1 (the coordinate map κ) and step 7 (transport of the carrier area formula). Notation: for x ∈ ℝ^P, T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x, (u_i) := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T_x indexed by Fin(dim T_x), J_F(x) := sqrt(det Γ_F(x)) with Γ_F(x)_ij := (DF(x)u_i)_1(DF(x)u_j)_1 + (DF(x)u_i)_2(DF(x)u_j)_2, where DF(x) := fderiv ℝ F x; volume on ℝ × ℝ is the product Lebesgue measure.
1. (Coordinates.) Let κ : ℝ × ℝ → Euclid 2 be the continuous linear equivalence sending p to the Euclidean vector with coordinates (p.1, p.2), i.e. κ := (ContinuousLinearEquiv.finTwoArrow ℝ ℝ).symm followed by (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 2) ℝ).symm; as a function κ = WithLp.toLp 2 ∘ MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow.symm. Since the inner product of Euclid 2 is the sum of the products of coordinates (`PiLp.inner_apply`, `Fin.sum_univ_two`), ⟨κ p, κ p'⟩ = p.1 p'.1 + p.2 p'.2 for all p, p' ∈ ℝ × ℝ.
2. (κ preserves Lebesgue measure.) MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ × ℝ is measure preserving for the volumes (`MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ`), so its inverse is measure preserving (`MeasurePreserving.symm`), and WithLp.toLp 2 : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → Euclid 2 is measure preserving (`PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp`). The composition κ is therefore measure preserving from (ℝ × ℝ, volume) to (Euclid 2, volume) (`MeasurePreserving.comp`). Being a homeomorphism, κ is a measurable embedding (`Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding`).
3. (The Euclid 2-valued map.) Put Φ := κ ∘ F : ℝ^P → Euclid 2. Since κ is a continuous linear map, Φ is C¹ on Z (`ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn`, i.e. κ.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn hF). For every x ∈ ℝ^P, fderiv ℝ Φ x = κ ∘L fderiv ℝ F x (`ContinuousLinearEquiv.comp_fderiv`; this holds at every point because κ is a continuous linear equivalence). Hence, by step 1, ⟨DΦ(x)v, DΦ(x)v'⟩ = (DF(x)v)_1(DF(x)v')_1 + (DF(x)v)_2(DF(x)v')_2 for all v, v', so for every x the Gram matrix ⟨DΦ(x)u_i, DΦ(x)u_j⟩ appearing in the carrier area formula equals Γ_F(x) entrywise and the two Jacobians coincide: J_Φ(x) = J_F(x).
4. (Fibres.) For p ∈ ℝ × ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P, Φ(x) = κ(p) iff F(x) = p, because κ is injective. Hence M ∩ Z ∩ Φ⁻¹{κ p} = M ∩ Z ∩ F⁻¹{p} as sets, and S_F(p) := Σ_{x ∈ M∩Z∩F⁻¹{p}} h(x) equals S_Φ(κ p), where S_Φ(y) := Σ_{x ∈ M∩Z∩Φ⁻¹{y}} h(x) (same index set and summands; rewrite the index set). Thus S_F = S_Φ ∘ κ.
5. (Area formula on the carrier.) Apply `Submission.idtp_carrier_area_formula` with n := 2 (so 1 ≤ n), the given M and Z, F := Φ and the given h. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumptions (M Borel, countably 2-rectifiable, μHE[2](M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K, Z open, h a.e.-measurable for μHE[2]⌞M) together with ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ Z from step 3. It yields: S_Φ is a.e.-measurable for volume on Euclid 2, and ∫ S_Φ d(volume) = ∫_{M∩Z} ofReal(sqrt(det ⟨DΦ(x)u_i, DΦ(x)u_j⟩))·h(x) dμHE[2](x).
6. (Transport.) By steps 2 and 4, S_F = S_Φ ∘ κ is a.e.-measurable for volume on ℝ × ℝ (`MeasurePreserving.aemeasurable_comp_iff` applied with the measurable embedding κ: AEMeasurable (S_Φ ∘ κ) ↔ AEMeasurable S_Φ), which is the first conjunct. Moreover ∫ S_F d(volume) = ∫ S_Φ(κ p) dp = ∫ S_Φ d(volume) (`MeasurePreserving.lintegral_comp_emb`, valid for every [0,∞]-valued function since κ is a measurable embedding). By step 5 and the pointwise identity J_Φ = J_F of step 3 (apply `lintegral_congr`), this equals ∫_{M∩Z} ofReal(J_F(x))·h(x) dμHE[2](x), the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: κ : ℝ×ℝ → Euclid 2, p ↦ (p.1, p.2), is a continuous linear equivalence with ⟨κp, κp'⟩ = p.1p'.1 + p.2p'.2, measure preserving (finTwoArrow.symm then toLp) and a measurable embedding.
Φ := κ ∘ F is C¹ on Z with fderiv Φ x = κ ∘L fderiv F x, so its Gram Jacobian equals the ℝ×ℝ Gram Jacobian of F at every x.
Fibres: M ∩ Z ∩ Φ⁻¹{κp} = M ∩ Z ∩ F⁻¹{p}, so the fibre sum of F is (fibre sum of Φ) ∘ κ.
Apply idtp_carrier_area_formula (n = 2) to Φ and transport a.e.-measurability and the lintegral along the measure-preserving embedding κ.
